Parthia: Historical region located in northeastern Iran. Parthia (Old Persian: 𐎱𐎼𐎰𐎺 Parθava; Parthian: 𐭐𐭓𐭕𐭅 Parθaw; Middle Persian: 𐭯𐭫𐭮𐭥𐭡𐭥 Pahlaw) is a historical region located in northeastern Greater Iran.

Its name comes from Ancient Greek for "love of wisdom," and once upon a time physics and psychology were considered branches of it before going their separate academic ways. What rational, critical field is this?
Philosophy: Study of general and fundamental questions.
Often depicted as a beautiful woman with butterfly wings, this mortal-turned-immortal endured trials set by Venus to win back her husband Cupid in Apuleius's The Golden Ass — who is she?
Psyche (mythology): Wife of Cupid. Psyche is known from the ancient Roman proto-novel The Golden Ass (also known as the Metamorphoses), written by philosopher and orator Apuleius in the 2nd century.
Trained as a lawyer, this conservative French statesman served three stints as prime minister before becoming president in 1913 — who is he?
Raymond Poincaré: President of France from 1913 to 1920.

Of Jewish descent, this Czechoslovak-born media baron escaped the Nazis, won a British Army decoration, served as a Labour MP, and built an empire that swallowed the Mirror Group and Macmillan — who was he?
Nicknamed Iran's 'hanging judge,' this cleric headed the country's revolutionary court from 1979 to 1981 and ordered the destruction of a former shah's mausoleum — who was he?
Sadegh Khalkhali: Iranian cleric and politician (1926–2003)
This Roman general's victory over Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC earned him an honorific epithet referencing the continent he conquered — who was he?
Scipio Africanus: Roman general and politician (236/235 – c. 183 BC)
Daughter of Bangladesh's first president, she became the country's longest-serving prime minister and one of the world's longest-serving female heads of government — who is she?
Sheikh Hasina: Prime Minister of Bangladesh (1996–2001; 2009–2024)
Established as a client state of Nazi Germany in March 1939, this Central European nation's army also joined the invasion of Poland that year — which state, whose capital was Bratislava?
Slovak Republic (1939–1945): Client state of Nazi Germany. The Slovak part of Czechoslovakia declared independence with German support one day before the German occupation of Bohemia and Moravia.
Established by Seljuk Turks after their victory over Byzantine forces at Manzikert in 1071, this Turco-Persian state is considered the beginning of Turkish history in Anatolia. What was it?
Sultanate of Rum: Turkish state in central Anatolia from 1077 to 1308.
Second only to Cameroon's leader in tenure among non-royal heads of state, this president has ruled Equatorial Guinea since ousting his uncle in a 1979 coup — who is he?
Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo: Dictator of Equatorial Guinea since 1979. Obiang was Chairperson of the African Union from 2011 to 2012.
Born in 1320, this ruler acceded to the throne in 1333 and became the last emperor of one dynasty and the first of its northern successor state after fleeing — who was he?
Toghon Temür: Emperor of Yuan dynasty from 1333 to 1368.
Head of state for nearly 26 years and often called an autocrat, this longest-serving Finnish president steered a policy of "active neutrality." Who was he?
Urho Kekkonen: President of Finland from 1956 to 1982.
Leading Russia's Liberal Democratic Party from 1992 until his death in 2022, this firebrand ran in nearly every presidential election and openly called for military action against NATO — who is he?
Once a loyal Nazi admiral running Germany's military intelligence service, he turned to sabotage and resistance against Hitler — and was hanged for treason at Flossenbürg in 1945. Who was he?

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
Pakistan's longest-serving de-facto ruler, this general seized power in a 1977 coup and held it until his death in a 1988 airplane crash — who is he?
Zia-ul-Haq: 6th President of Pakistan from 1978 to 1988.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
John Archibald Wheeler is a physicist. John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 – April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Joseph Liouville is a mathematician. The crater Liouville on the Moon is named after him.
What is the atomic number of Bohrium?
Bohrium: Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
What is the atomic number of Platinum?
Platinum: Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
In what year was Kalpana Chawla born?
Kalpana Chawla: Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 – February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
In what year was Peter Piot born?
Peter Piot: Sir Peter Karel, Baron Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.
In what year was Ibn Khaldun born?
Ibn Khaldun: Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 – 17 March 1406, 732–808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
In what year did H. H. Holmes die?
H. H. Holmes: Holmes, was an American con artist and serial killer active between 1891 and 1894.
In what year did Dmitri Mendeleev die?
Dmitri Mendeleev: The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
In what year was Magnesium discovered?
Magnesium: Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
Adenosine: Pfizer. Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
In which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 based?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet Union. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
Who is credited with discovering Niobium?
Niobium: Charles Hatchett. Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
Who is credited with discovering Peroxisome?
Peroxisome: Christian de Duve. A peroxisome is a membrane-bound organelle, a type of microbody, found in the cytoplasm of virtually all eukaryotic cells.
Who is credited with discovering Uncertainty principle?
Uncertainty principle: Werner Heisenberg. The uncertainty principle, also known as Heisenberg's indeterminacy principle, is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics.
Who is credited with discovering Mensa?
Mensa (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is Latin for table, though it originally commemorated Table Mountain and was known as "Mons Mensae".

Belonging to the birch family and numbering about 35 species, these monoecious trees and shrubs are found across the north temperate zone, with a few extending into Central America and the Andes — name this genus of tree?
Alder are trees of the genus Alnus in the birch family Betulaceae.

Affecting roughly 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder impairs the nervous system, causing severe intellectual disability and little to no speech, but is also linked to an unusually happy demeanor — what's it called?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
This large bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet consists mostly — 70 to 90 percent — of bone. What bird is it?
Bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.

This general medical term describes blood escaping a damaged vessel, whether internally or through a puncture in the skin, with the loss of more than about 15 percent of total volume proving potentially fatal. What is it called?
Bleeding is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.

Naturally green and yellow with scalloped black markings, this small, long-tailed seed-eating parrot native to Australia is bred worldwide in colors from blue to white — which bird, also called a budgie?
Budgerigar (--ree-; Melopsittacus undulatus), also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie, is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia.

Which German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist discovered oxygen — though Priestley published first — and identified elements like molybdenum, tungsten, and chlorine before reportedly dying of mercury poisoning?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele (9 December 1742 - 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.
A sweet-smelling, dense, colorless liquid with the formula CHCl3, this solvent doubled as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century into the early 20th. What is it?
Chloroform (often abbreviated as TCM), is an organochloride with the formula CHCl3 and a common solvent.

This icy small body from the outer Solar System develops a glowing atmosphere called a coma, and sometimes a tail, as it warms and releases gases when passing near the Sun — name this celestial object?
Comet is an icy, small Solar System body or interstellar object that warms and begins to release gases when passing close to the Sun, a process called outgassing.
This bird family, the sole one in its taxonomic order, includes roadrunners, koels, malkohas, and coucals across roughly 150 species. Name the family?
Cuckoo are birds in the family Cuculidae, the sole taxon in the order Cuculiformes.
Mother of Princess Alia, this royal later remarried a senior PLO official in 1970 after her short-lived marriage to Jordan's king ended — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid (15 December 1929 - 21 August 2019) was a Hashemite princess and Queen of Jordan from 1955 until 1957 as the first wife of King Hussein.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

Combining lab and field science with strong ties to ecology and evolutionary biology, this discipline earned three of its founders a shared 1973 Nobel Prize for their work on animal behavior — what field is it?
Ethology is a branch of zoology that studies the behaviour of non-human animals.
Discovered in 1999 at a Dubna lab, this synthetic superheavy element (symbol Fl, number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name was transliterated from Cyrillic — which element?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
This field of study examines how a country's physical geography shapes its politics and its relations with other nations — what field is it?
Geopolitics (from Ancient Greek g 'earth, land' and politik 'politics') is the study of the effects of Earth's geography on politics and international relations.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This occupation and set of methods involves producing and distributing reports on events and people that make up the 'news of the day,' with a commitment to accuracy — what is it?
Journalism is the production and distribution of reports on events, facts, ideas, and people that constitute the "news of the day" and inform society with a commitment to accuracy and verification.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally grouped under a nickname referencing marital loss, encompassing both black and brown members — what is its scientific name?
Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
Known mainly from fossils in Peru's Pisco Formation, this Miocene-era macroraptorial sperm whale takes its name from a biblical sea monster — what is it called?
Livyatan is an extinct genus of highly predatory macroraptorial sperm whale, containing one known species: L. melvillei.
Its Spanish name translates to 'little apple of death' — this tropical tree's apple-like fruit and toxic milky sap make it one of the most poisonous trees on Earth — which tree?
Manchineel (Hippomane mancinella), also known as the tree of death, is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family (Euphorbiaceae).
Home to a relativistic plasma jet stretching nearly 5,000 light-years from its core, this giant elliptical galaxy sits in the constellation Virgo — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87 (also known as Virgo A or NGC 4486, generally abbreviated to M87) is a supergiant elliptical galaxy in the constellation Virgo that contains several trillion stars.
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
This Persian polymath and poet was the first to provide a general geometric solution to all third-degree polynomial equations, using the intersection of conic sections. Who is he?
Omar Khayyam (1048-1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
This galliform game bird, native to Europe, Asia, and Africa, was once lumped in with pheasants and quail, but DNA suggests it isn't one distinct group at all — which bird is it?
Partridge is a medium-sized galliform bird in any of several genera, with a wide native distribution throughout parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

Named early in the history of microbiology for its widespread presence in water and plant seeds, which genus of gram-negative bacteria includes an opportunistic human pathogen infamous in hospitals as well as plant and soil-dwelling species?
Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.

Known from complete specimens found in Bolivia, this extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period resembled a slender tadpole with eyes set like car headlamps on its oversized head — what is it?
Sacabambaspis is an extinct genus of armored jawless fish which lived in the Ordovician period.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Mostly made from potato starch but also lurking in apples and berries, this slowly-metabolized sugar alcohol is an isomer of mannitol, differing only by one hydroxyl group's orientation — what is it?
Sorbitol is a sugar alcohol with a sweet taste which the human body metabolizes slowly.
This small nocturnal marsupial sails between trees on membranes stretched from wrist to ankle, and its Latin name translates as 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider (Petaurus breviceps) is a small, omnivorous, arboreal, and nocturnal gliding possum.

This family of marine and freshwater fish can inflate themselves dramatically, revealing thin spines that stay hidden against their skin until they puff up — unlike their spinier, porcupine-like relatives — name this fish family?
Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.

Stretching from the base of the skull down to the lower back and out to each shoulder blade, this large paired muscle supports the arm and moves the scapula in three distinct ways — what's the muscle?
Trapezius is a large paired trapezoid-shaped surface muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae of the spine and laterally to the spine of the scapula.

Named after an 18th-century Italian physicist and first published in 1797, this phenomenon explains why fluid pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrower pipe section — powering wine aerators and vacuum ejectors. What is it called?
Venturi effect is the reduction in fluid pressure that results when a moving fluid speeds up as it is funneled from one section of a pipe to another, smaller section.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas packs all four of its atoms into one straight line thanks to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and fuels welding torches — which compound is it?
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this soft-spoken economist logged the second-longest tenure ever as chairman of the Federal Reserve — who was he?
Alan Greenspan: American economist and financial advisor (born 1926)
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
Named from Greek words for 'curved' and 'vertebra,' this type of arthritis causes long-term inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis — what is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis: Type of arthritis of the spine. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
The fourth-brightest star in the night sky and the brightest in the northern hemisphere, this aging red giant in Boötes has ballooned to 25 times the Sun's size despite sharing its mass — what is it?
Arcturus: Brightest star in the constellation Boötes. It has the Bayer designation α Boötis, which is Latinized to Alpha Boötis and abbreviated Alpha Boo or α Boo.
This independent examination of financial records culminates in a report expressing an opinion on whether the books are free of material misstatement — what is it called?
Audit: Independent examination of an organization. The term is most frequently applied to audits of the financial information relating to a legal person.
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.
Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, this astronomical body is so compact that not even light can escape past its event horizon. What is it?
Black hole: Compact astronomical body. A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.

This rare and potentially fatal illness comes from a toxin better known by its cosmetic nickname; it starts with blurry vision and slurred speech but usually spares both fever and consciousness — what is it?
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
Tetravalent and able to form four covalent bonds, this element known since antiquity ranks as the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass — which one is it?
Carbon: Chemical element with atomic number 6 (C)

Greek for "head-feet," fishers nickname these inkfish for their ink-squirting trick; their arms are muscular hydrostats modified from the primitive molluscan foot. Which marine class includes the octopus, squid, and nautilus?
Cephalopod: Class of mollusks. The study of cephalopods is a branch of malacology known as teuthology.
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
A tropane alkaloid drawn from the leaves of South American coca plants, it once served doctors as a local anesthetic with handy vasoconstricting properties — what is this stimulant?

Cocaine: Tropane alkaloid and stimulant drug. The leaves are processed into cocaine paste, a crude mixture of coca alkaloids, from which cocaine base is isolated and then converted to cocaine hydrochloride.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.

Named after a mythological Greek youth transformed into a tree after killing his pet stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is found across warm temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Cupressus: Several genera of evergreen conifers.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
This American astronomer proved that many so-called nebulae were actually separate galaxies, and in 1929 showed that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are — who is he?
Triggered by the parasympathetic nervous system and a rise in nitric oxide, this physiological event leaves an organ firm and engorged — what is it?
Erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the hardening and enlargement of the penis.

Also known as the wisent, this species is the heaviest wild land mammal on its continent — hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 20th century before being restored through captive breeding programs. Which animal?
European bison: Eurasian species of mammal. It is one of two extant species of bison, alongside the American bison.
Born Leonardo Bonacci in Pisa, this medieval Italian mathematician's 1202 book 'Liber Abaci' introduced Europe to Indo-Arabic numerals and a famous number sequence bearing his nickname — who is he?
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
Pioneered by Gregor Mendel's 19th-century pea plant experiments in Brno, this branch of biology studies heredity and trait inheritance — what is it?
Genetics: Science of genes, heredity and variation.
First selectively bred for color in imperial China over 1,000 years ago, which popular aquarium pet has become an invasive pest after being released into rivers in North America and Australia?
Goldfish: Freshwater fish common in aquariums.
Making its first flight in 2001 and entering Indian Air Force service in 2015, this delta-wing multirole fighter is the smallest and lightest supersonic jet of its generation — which aircraft?
HAL Tejas: Indian combat aircraft. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Once down to just 94 individuals in Andalusia by 2002, largely due to a crash in its rabbit prey from myxomatosis, this medium-sized wild cat is endemic to a European peninsula — which species?
Iberian lynx: Species of mammal. The Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus) is one of four extant species of Lynx, a genus of medium-sized wild cats.
This 12th-century polymath from Mesopotamia wrote a treatise describing 50 ingenious mechanical devices, including his famous elephant clock, earning him the title 'father of robotics' — who is he?
Ismail al-Jazari: Muslim engineer and artist (1136–1206)
As chief engineer, this man designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero, Japan's iconic World War II fighter plane, and later worked on the postwar NAMC YS-11 airliner — who is he?
A founder of modern geometric analysis, this American mathematician won the 2019 Abel Prize for pioneering work in geometric partial differential equations and gauge theory — who is she?
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.

Nicknamed the 'leopard slug' for its spotted grey-brown skin, this mollusc mates by dangling from a thread of mucus off a tree branch — which species, first spotted outside Europe in Philadelphia in 1867?
Limax maximus: Species of slug. It is among the largest keeled slugs, Limax cinereoniger being the largest.
As West Germany's economics minister, he engineered the postwar 'Wirtschaftswunder' before becoming the country's second chancellor in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard: Chancellor of West Germany from 1963 to 1966.

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
